saints.name: St. Vincent de Paul
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The Gascon priest who organized the charity of an age, gathering priests and laywomen to serve the poor, the galley-slave, and the foundling…
biography: Born to a peasant family in Gascony in 1581, Vincent was ordained young and, after a conversion to deeper zeal, gave his life to the poor. In 1625 he founded the Congregation of the Mission (the Vincentians) to preach in the countryside and form clergy, and organized parish charities across France.

With St. Louise de Marillac he founded the Daughters of Charity, sending sisters into the streets and hospitals, and he laboured for galley-slaves, abandoned children, and the victims of war. He died in 1660 and was canonized in 1737; his name remains a byword for organized Christian charity.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Vincentians and Daughters of Charity for the service of the poor.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 September
